the activation of Raf-1 signaling suppresses the production of neuro-endocrine markers and cellular migration in carcinoid cells.

the role of Raf-1 signaling pathway in carcinoid cells.
the mechanisms by which Raf1 regulates the neuroendocrine (NE) markers and the metastatic properties of BON carcinoid cells.
the mechanisms by which Raf1/MEK/ERK signaling cascade mediates changes in the neuro-endocrine phenotype in carcinoid cells and how the FAK protein is a key mediator of these changes.

Raf-1 activation in BON carcinoid cells induced the phosphorylation of Focal Adhesion Kinases (FAK) at the Tyr407 residues, which in turn suppressed the neuroendocrine markers (chromogranin A and serotonin) and reduced cellular adhesion and motility.

Raf-1 activation in carcinoid cells leads to a decrease in the neuroendrocrine markers, which is mediated through FAK activation and phosphorylation at Tyr407.

the Raf-1/MAPK signaling cascade plays a critical role in regulating neuroendocrine and malignant properties of carcinoid tumor cells, and that FAK may be an important downstream mediator of Raf-1 signaling in carcinoid tumors.

the Raf-1 kinase is a key regulator of cellular adhesion, migration, and neuroendocrine markers in BON carcinoid cells.
